title: Characteristic-zero Dedekind domains are excellent
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is integrally closed in its fraction field $K$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and suppose every nonzero prime ideal of $A$ is maximal. If $K$ has characteristic zero, then $A$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Fields are included. In particular, every discrete valuation ring $R$ whose fraction field has characteristic zero is excellent; a discrete valuation ring has the equivalent local principal-ideal and Noetherian local dimension-one forms of [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. No completeness, henselianity, or finite-type hypothesis over $\mathbf Z$ is required.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, clauses (4) (Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero) and (1) (fields). The DVR specialization uses Algebra Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, equivalence (1)/(4)/(5).

proof.text: For every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ has length one, and no prime chain can have length two because every nonzero prime is maximal. Thus $\dim A=1$ whenever such a prime exists. Apply [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr] with $B=A$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p$: all its Noetherianity, normality, dimension-one and maximality hypotheses hold. Therefore $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a DVR. At $(0)$ the fraction description of localization gives $A_{(0)}=K$. Each $A_{\mathfrak p}$ has fraction field $K$: inside $K$ a fraction of localized elements is $(a/s)/(b/t)=at/(sb)$, and every $a/b\in K$ is $(a/1)/(b/1)$.

source.place: Tag 034X, lemma-characterize-Dedekind, (3) implies (2), with the zero prime treated separately.

proof.text: Every localization in step 1 is regular local. For a DVR its maximal ideal is principal and it is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; its dimension is one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one]. Hence its maximal ideal is generated by exactly the number of elements required in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $A_{(0)}=K$, use [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Consequently $A$ is a Noetherian regular ring.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, (1) implies (3); Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; Tag 00OD, definition-regular.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary] to $A$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given Noetherianity and the regularity of every prime localization proved in step 2. Thus $A$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, proof: regular rings are universally catenary, by Algebra Tags 00NM (lemma-CM-ring-catenary) and 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM).

proof.text: For every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$, step 1 gives a Noetherian local DVR $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with characteristic-zero fraction field $K$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-completion-regular] makes its completion map regular. At $(0)$ the local ring is $K$, whose zero-adic completion is $K$ itself: the inverse system $K/(0)^n$ is constant for $n\geq1$. The completion map is the identity. This map is flat because tensoring along the identity is the identity functor; its only fibre is $K$, geometrically regular over itself since every finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$ gives the field $L\otimes_KK=L$, regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Thus every prime-local completion map is regular, which, together with Noetherianity, is exactly the G-ring definition [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Tag 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, proof for (1) and (4); Tag 07GH, definition-G-ring; Tag 07BZ, definition-regular.

proof.text: Check [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion] for $R=A$. Given a prime $\mathfrak p$ and a finite purely inseparable $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, there are two cases. If $\mathfrak p=(0)$, then $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=K$ has characteristic zero, so $L=K$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Take $B=A\subseteq K$: it is generated by $1$ as an $A$-module, its fraction field is $K=L$, and its whole spectrum is a nonempty regular open by step 2 (it contains $(0)$). If $\mathfrak p\ne(0)$ it is maximal, so $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A/\mathfrak p$. Take $B=L\subseteq L$. A finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-basis of $L$ also generates it over $A$, because every coefficient lifts along the surjection $A\to A/\mathfrak p$. Its fraction field is $L$, and its whole spectrum is nonempty and regular by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. All hypotheses of the criterion hold; hence $A$ is J-2.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof for (6) using Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, condition (4).

proof.text: The ring $A$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, universally catenary by step 3, a G-ring by step 4, and J-2 by step 5. These are exactly the four conditions of [def-exc-excellent-ring], so $A$ is excellent. This also covers fields: all the preceding zero-prime cases apply without requiring a nonzero prime.

Finally let $R$ be the DVR in the last clause. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] it is a local principal ideal domain, so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] gives Noetherianity and integral closedness. By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] its dimension is one. Every nonzero prime is maximal: a strict inclusion of a nonzero prime into the unique maximal ideal would give a chain of length two beginning at $(0)$, contrary to dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus $R$ satisfies all the hypotheses just used for $A$, and its characteristic-zero fraction field gives excellence. No additional hypothesis has entered.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q158-9b3c55975 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full 7-step split, every cited statement, and the Stacks source (more-algebra.tex 07QW l.13386, 07PX l.12652, 07PJ l.11945, 07PC l.11689 condition (4)). The delivery has no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. proof_deps is exactly the union of the step citations, and there is no cycle. Step 1: when a nonzero prime exists, dim A = 1, so lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr applies; Frac(A_p) = K. Step 2: a DVR is regular local, and K is regular by the field node. Step 3: the regular-ring universal-catenarity hypotheses hold. Step 4: G-ring at a nonzero prime by lem-weil-pbc-dvr-completion-regular, whose characteristic-zero fraction-field hypothesis is checked; the zero prime is handled through the trivial completion of K. Step 5: the J-2 criterion holds with B=A at (0), where L=K in characteristic 0, and with B=L at a maximal p, finite over A by lifting a basis. Steps 6 and 7 assemble the result and give the DVR specialization. This writes out the Dedekind case that 07PJ leaves unwritten. Small cases checked: Q, Z_(p), Z_p and Z. The characteristic-zero hypothesis is genuinely used. The three off-unit tools are declared in split_report.tool_uses and are generic commutative algebra, so I accept them. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary (closure: CM/polynomial algebra only) and lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion (reaches only lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula) are pure commutative algebra and no part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accept both. No changes.
